rules.advice: Give the page a title, with the main subject first, inside the length range.
Write a meta description inside the length range, one sentence that makes a reader want to click.
Remove noindex from the robots meta tag, unless the page must stay out of search results.
Remove nofollow from the robots meta tag, so that search engines follow the links of the page.
Declare a canonical URL, so that one page reached at several addresses counts as one page.
Give the page an Open Graph title and image, which a social network shows when the page is shared.
Add JSON-LD structured data that states what the page is about.
Fix the JSON-LD blocks that do not parse, because a search engine ignores them.
Declare the language of the page on the html element.
Make the language of the html element match the language of the content.
Give every image an alt attribute: a description, or an empty value for a decorative image.
Replace link labels such as "click here" with words that say where the link goes.
Give the page exactly one H1 heading, which names its main subject.
Fix the connection from the Jahia server to the public address of the page.
Let every AI crawler get the page: a refusal usually comes from a firewall or a bot-protection rule.
Make robots.txt and the server agree on which crawlers may read the page.
Replace the meta refresh with a server redirect, which a crawler follows.
Name the AI crawlers in robots.txt, so that the site takes an explicit decision about them.
Let a visitor with no account read the page, or accept that no crawler will.
Render the text of the page on the server, because a crawler does not run JavaScript.
Serve a crawler the same text as a browser: check what the server varies on the user agent.
Split the page with H2 headings, because retrieval splits a page on its headings.
Publish the modification date of the page, so that an assistant can tell it is current.
Describe the images in their alt text, because a crawler that reads only text does not see them.
Serve a robots.txt file, so that the site decides what crawlers may read.
Serve an llms.txt file that tells an assistant which pages matter and why.
Shorten the sentences and use everyday words: the text is very hard to read.
Shorten the longest sentences and replace jargon: the text is hard to read.
Split the sentences that are longer than the limit.
Split the paragraphs, whose average length is over the limit.
Do not skip a heading level, such as an H4 right after an H2.
Expand the page or merge it into another one: a short page informs and ranks poorly.
Reduce what the page downloads: images, scripts and fonts.
Reduce the number of files the page requests.
Simplify the markup of the page, whose number of elements is over the limit.
Load the images below the fold lazily.
Serve images in WebP or AVIF instead of JPEG, PNG or GIF.
Serve each image at the size the page shows it.
Give each image its width and height, so that the page does not move while it loads.
Load fewer font files, in WOFF2.
Do not start a video or a sound on its own.
Load files from fewer third-party hosts.
Split or reduce the scripts and stylesheets that are over the limit.
Fix or remove the links that lead to an error.
Link to a page of the site through Jahia, not through a typed address.
Load every resource of an HTTPS page over HTTPS.
Add rel="noopener" to the links that open a new tab.
Add the missing labels to the resource bundles, because visitors see the technical key.
Publish the content of the page that changed since the last publication.
Translate the content of the page into the languages of the site.
Replace the placeholder text, such as lorem ipsum or TODO.
Make the GraphQL API of Jahia answer, so that the content checks can run.
